page: Microsoft Azure F2als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 2 dedicated x86_64 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz, configured with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is fixed at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The CPU architecture incorporates 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), SHA-NI, and VAES. The instance does not include bundled local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and it contains no discrete graphics hardware.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core compute performance alongside predictable constraints in aggregate multi-threaded execution. The instance scores 2049.0 in Geekbench single-core and 3079.28 in stress-ng single-core tests, placing in the top quartile of evaluated systems. Text processing capabilities also register in the upper tier. However, overall multi-core throughput reflects the small two-core footprint, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 3749.0 and PassMark CPU reaching 5405.05. Memory bandwidth reaches 39.5 GB/sec for large block reads and 28.11 GB/sec for writes, supporting single-threaded gzip compression at 29.48 GB/sec and lightweight LLM inference on small 135M parameter models.

The qualitative tradeoff of the F2als_v6 centers on high per-core execution efficiency at a low aggregate resource footprint. Because physical cores are dedicated without simultaneous multithreading overhead, individual processing threads achieve reliable throughput without resource contention. However, the 4.0 GB memory envelope and absence of local storage make the instance unsuitable for large in-memory caches, heavy database operations, or memory-intensive compilation tasks. The instance functions best for single-threaded batch processing, lightweight microservices, monitoring agents, and low-concurrency network tasks requiring modern instruction sets and high clock speeds.
description: Microsoft Azure F2als_v6 is a compute-optimized instance offering 2 dedicated x86_64 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz with 1 thread per core. It provides 4.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 compute-to-memory profile, with 32 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark data demonstrates strong single-core CPU execution, achieving top-quartile results in single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside average memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks. Aggregate multi-core throughput and database metric scores are naturally limited by the two-core allocation. The F2als_v6 is well suited for lightweight compute tasks, small batch processing jobs, API gateways, and microservices requiring dedicated per-core clock speed without substantial memory overhead.
